```{r setup}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 13))
d <- "huehue_union"
runs <- c(A = "alone", B = "+ parviglumis", C = "+ mexicana")
hue <- c("Zh.0020_P3", "Zh.0030_P4")
markers <- fread(file.path(d, "markers.tsv"))[, union := runs[run]]
checks <- rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(r) {
  rbindlist(lapply(list.files(file.path(d, r), "line_checks.tsv$", full.names = TRUE), function(f) {
    fread(f, na.strings = ".")[, `:=`(run = r, donor = sub("\\.chr10.*", "", basename(f)))]
  }))
}))
# sample introgression dosage check on per-donor medians (docs/decisions.md 2026-10-11, criteria 1-2)
dose <- checks[, .(
  samples = .N, segs_median = median(n_donor_segments), segs_max = max(n_donor_segments),
  ref = median(ref_alt_pct, na.rm = TRUE), het = median(het_alt_pct, na.rm = TRUE), alt = median(alt_alt_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(run, donor)]
dose[, balanced := segs_median <= 4 & (is.na(ref) | ref <= 3) & (is.na(het) | (het >= 30 & het <= 55)) &
  (is.na(alt) | alt >= 75)]
seg <- rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(r) {
  rbindlist(lapply(hue, function(h) fread(file.path(d, r, paste0(h, ".segments.bed")))[, `:=`(run = r, donor = h)]))
}))
setnames(seg, "#chrom", "chrom", skip_absent = TRUE)
shares <- seg[, .(bp = sum(end - start)), by = .(run, donor, line, state)][
  , .(het = sum(bp[state == 1]) / sum(bp), alt = sum(bp[state == 2]) / sum(bp)),
  by = .(run, donor, line)
]
snp <- fread(file.path(d, "snp50k_chr10_huehue.csv"))
snp_shares <- snp[, .(bp = sum(end_bp - start_bp)), by = .(line = name, state)][
  , .(het = sum(bp[state == 1]) / sum(bp), alt = sum(bp[state == 2]) / sum(bp)),
  by = line
]
```

## Why

User, 2026-10-16: whether *Z. mays* ssp. *huehuetenangensis* (2 donors, 9 BC1 pools, 61 BC2S3 samples) gets its own
union or joins another taxon's ("we need data to have a decision"). Chen et al. (2022) Fig. 2a source data:
F~ST~ huehuetenangensis–parviglumis 0.200, –mexicana 0.248, –maize 0.330; mexicana–parviglumis 0.068. Run plan:
`docs/runs/genotype_huehue_chr10.md`. Collected by `agent/huehue_chr10/collect.sh` (log there); this notebook reads only
the extracted tables in `huehue_union/`.

## 1. Markers per donor

A donor's RTIGER markers are the union sites gap filling calls ALT for it: its own tier-A sites plus gap-filled sites
from the other donors of the same union (Milestone 9a).

```{r markers}
knitr::kable(markers[, .(union, donor, union_sites, tier_a, union_alt, own, gap_filled)],
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  col.names = c("union", "donor", "union sites", "tier-A sites", "markers (union-ALT)", "own", "gap-filled")
)
```

## 2. Calls: the sample introgression dosage check

Per donor, medians over its BC2S3 samples: donor segments per sample and ALT % of reads in REF / HET / ALT segments.
A family has balanced tissue pools when the medians pass (at most 4 segments; REF <= 3 %, HET 30-55 %, ALT >= 75 %).

```{r dosage}
knitr::kable(dose[donor %in% hue][order(donor, run), .(
  donor, union = runs[run], samples, segs_median, segs_max, ref, het, alt,
  tissue_pools = fifelse(balanced, "balanced", "unbalanced")
)], digits = 1, col.names = c(
  "donor", "union", "samples", "segments, median", "segments, max", "REF % ALT", "HET % ALT", "ALT % ALT",
  "tissue pools"
))
```

## 3. Genotype classes

Share of chr10 called HET and donor per BC2S3 sample, against the single-locus BC2S2 expectation (HET 6.25 %, donor
9.4 %) and the SNP50K calls of the same samples.

```{r classes}
pipe_cls <- shares[, .(het = mean(het), alt = mean(alt), samples = .N), by = .(run, donor)]
pipe_cls[, source := paste("union", runs[run])]
snp_cls <- snp_shares[shares[run == "A", .(line, donor)], on = "line", nomatch = NULL][
  , .(het = mean(het), alt = mean(alt), samples = .N),
  by = donor
][, source := "SNP50K"]
cls <- rbind(pipe_cls[, .(donor, source, samples, het, alt)], snp_cls[, .(donor, source, samples, het, alt)])
knitr::kable(cls[order(donor, source), .(donor, source, samples, het = 100 * het, donor_class = 100 * alt)],
  digits = 1, col.names = c("donor", "calls", "samples", "HET % of chr10", "donor % of chr10")
)
```

## 4. What adding huehuetenangensis does to the partner taxon

```{r partner}
mex_old <- rbindlist(lapply(list.files("huehue_union/mexicana_1273053", "line_checks.tsv$", full.names = TRUE), function(f) {
  fread(f, na.strings = ".")[, donor := sub("\\.chr10.*", "", basename(f))]
}))[, .(segs_old = median(n_donor_segments), het_old = median(het_alt_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
       alt_old = median(alt_alt_pct, na.rm = TRUE)), by = donor]
mex_new <- dose[run == "C" & !donor %in% hue, .(donor, segs_new = segs_median, het_new = het, alt_new = alt)]
cmp <- mex_old[mex_new, on = "donor", nomatch = NULL]
knitr::kable(cmp[, .(
  donors = .N,
  `segments: changed donors` = sum(segs_old != segs_new),
  `HET % ALT: max change` = max(abs(het_new - het_old), na.rm = TRUE),
  `ALT % ALT: max change` = max(abs(alt_new - alt_old), na.rm = TRUE)
)], digits = 1, caption = "Mexicana donors' line-check medians, run C against run 1273053 (mexicana alone)")
```

Run B is the first parviglumis run, so it has no parviglumis-only baseline to compare with.

## 5. Chromosome painting: SNP50K, the union alone and the union with parviglumis

One row per BC2S3 sample, grouped by donor; chr10 along the x axis. Left: SNP50K calls (RTIGER on the 50K panel);
middle: RTIGER at the union-ALT markers of the huehuetenangensis-only union (run A); right: the union with the 40
parviglumis donors (run B).

```{r painting, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 9}
# the style of agent/genochr10/dip_plots/fig1_paint_columns.R: rows per sample, REF gold, HET springgreen4, ALT purple4
paint <- rbind(
  snp[, .(source = "SNP50K", line = name, start = start_bp, end = end_bp, state)],
  seg[run == "A", .(source = "union alone", line, start, end, state)],
  seg[run == "B", .(source = "union + parviglumis", line, start, end, state)]
)
paint <- unique(shares[run == "A", .(line, donor)])[paint, on = "line", nomatch = NULL]
paint[, row := match(line, rev(sort(unique(line)))), by = donor]
paint[, state := factor(state, levels = 0:2, labels = c("REF", "HET", "ALT"))]
paint[, source := factor(source, levels = c("SNP50K", "union alone", "union + parviglumis"))]
paint[, label := paste0(donor, "\n", uniqueN(line), " lines"), by = donor]
ggplot(paint) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start / 1e6, xmax = end / 1e6, ymin = row - 0.48, ymax = row + 0.48, fill = state)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(REF = "gold", HET = "springgreen4", ALT = "purple4"), name = "State") +
  facet_grid(label ~ source, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "chr10 ancestry per line, huehuetenangensis (RTIGER per donor, same lines)",
       x = "chr10 position (Mb)", y = "lines") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0), strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.spacing.y = unit(4, "pt"))
```

## 6. Notes (2026-10-16)

- **Union alone fragments.** With only 2 donors the union is thin (68,177 sites; 52-56 k markers per donor); RTIGER
  breaks two samples into many pieces (SID806, SID846). Either partner union (+ parviglumis 464,813 sites, + mexicana
  410,196) doubles the markers, mostly gap-filled, and both samples become clean segments placed as SNP50K places them.
- **The partner taxon makes no difference here.** Runs B and C agree on segments, class shares and dosage medians for
  both donors. The data give no reason to prefer parviglumis (F~ST~ 0.200) over mexicana (0.248).
- **Proposal (user, 2026-10-16): one union of the three annual *Z. mays* subspecies** (mexicana, parviglumis,
  huehuetenangensis). Open: it changes mexicana's and parviglumis's own calls too (run C already moved 3 of 42 mexicana
  donors' segment counts); not yet tested as one run.
- **Confidence in why partners help is low.** Both partners are large and both are annual *Z. mays*, so "many donors"
  and "related donors" are confounded, and the mechanism (marker density or better gap-filling priors) is not
  separated; two fragmented samples in two families. Tests that would separate them: huehuetenangensis with
  diploperennis (distant), and with ~6 mexicana donors (few, close).
- **SNP50K calls donor-homozygous segments HET** (Zh.0020_P3: SNP50K HET 10.7 % / donor 0.1 %; unions 4.6-5.6 % /
  6.8-7.1 %; BC2S2 expectation 6.25 % / 9.4 %), as its diluted donor state predicts (diagnosis 2026-10-15, §4).
- **Zh.0030_P4** carries almost no introgression on chr10 (median 0 donor segments in every call set); its few
  "donor" calls in the union alone are short segments at 0-2 Mb, where SNP50K calls short HET segments.

Pairwise F~ST~ between the ZEAL taxa (Chen et al. 2022, Fig. 2a source data, five samples per taxon): parviglumis is
the nearest taxon to every other one (huehuetenangensis 0.200, diploperennis 0.230, luxurians 0.235, mexicana 0.068);
diploperennis and luxurians are far from each other (0.453) and from huehuetenangensis (0.48). Next: the same test for
diploperennis (`docs/runs/genotype_diploperennis_partners_chr10.md`).
